title: Even and odd integers
competency: Describe and identify even and odd integers, and their sums, differences and products.

keywords.def: An integer that 2 divides with no remainder, like −4, 0, 6.
An integer that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, like −3, 1, 5.
Integers that follow one another. Consecutive even integers differ by 2.

en.text: An even integer can be divided by 2 with no remainder. An odd integer leaves remainder 1. Look at the last digit: 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 means even; otherwise odd. Zero is even. Consecutive even or odd integers differ by 2.

screens.title: Pairs
screens.ask: Group 5 books in twos. What happens?
screens.after:
Make pairs: 2 + 2 = 4 books. 5 − 4 = 1 book is left over.
A number that leaves 1 over is odd. So 5 is odd.
6 balls make 3 pairs exactly, so 6 is even.

screens.title: Even and odd
paras: An even integer can be divided by 2 without a remainder.
An odd integer cannot be divided by 2. Its remainder is 1.

screens.title: Even, odd, even, odd …

points.info: Odd: 1 is left over after pairing.
Odd: one pair and 1 left over.

screens.ask: Tap the points. Even and odd take turns along the line.

screens.title: Many digits
paras: If the unit digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, the number is even.
Otherwise it is odd. So −252 is even and 345 is odd.
The next three even integers after 31 are 32, 34 and 36.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An integer that 2 divides with no remainder.
An integer that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2.

screens.text: Even or odd: is −252 even or odd?
screens.why:
Look at the unit (last) digit only: −252 ends in 2.
2 is one of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.
So −252 is even. The minus sign does not matter.
Check: −252 ÷ 2 = −126, no remainder.
screens.clue: Look at the last digit only.

screens.why:
Look at the unit digit of each number.
Ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8: even. So −36, 0 and −180 are even.
Ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9: odd. So 55, −71 and 103 are odd.
The sign does not change even or odd.
screens.title: Even or odd? Sort each integer.

screens.ask: Next even integer: the first even integer greater than 143 is ___
screens.why:
143 ends in 3, so it is odd.
The next integer is 143 + 1 = 144.
144 ends in 4, so it is even.
So the first even integer greater than 143 is 144.

screens.text: Consecutive odd integers: tap the next three odd integers greater than −54.
screens.why:
Greater than −54 means to the right of −54.
−54 is even, so the next integer, −53, is odd.
Odd integers are 2 apart: −53, −51, −49.
−55 is less than −54, so leave it out.
screens.clue: Greater means to the right of −54.

screens.ask: Two-digit integers: what is the smallest two-digit negative integer? ___
screens.why:
Two-digit negative integers go from −10 down to −99.
The smallest is furthest left on the number line.
−99 is furthest left.
−10 is the greatest two-digit negative integer, not the smallest.
screens.clue: Smallest means furthest left on the number line.

ideas.name: Adding, subtracting and multiplying even and odd

en.text: Even plus even is even, and odd plus odd is even. Even plus odd is odd. Subtraction follows the same pattern. A product is odd only when every factor is odd; one even factor makes it even.

screens.title: Odd + odd
screens.ask: Add two odd numbers: 31 + 25. Is the sum even or odd?
screens.after:
31 + 25 = 56.
56 ends in 6, so it is even.
Why: the two odd numbers each have 1 left over after pairing. The two leftovers make a new pair.
So odd + odd is always even.

screens.title: Even and odd results
screens.ask: Tap each operation to see the result and an example.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Integers that follow one another. Consecutive even integers differ by 2.

screens.text: Product of odd numbers: odd × odd = ?
screens.why:
Try an example: 5 × 3 = 15.
15 ends in 5, so it is odd.
Another: −9 × (−5) = 45, odd.
An odd number of odd groups always leaves 1 over. So odd × odd = odd.

even + even: 2 + 4 = 6, even.
even − odd: 4 − 1 = 3, odd.
odd × even: 3 × 2 = 6, even.
odd × odd: 3 × 5 = 15, odd.
screens.text: Even and odd results: match each operation with its result.

screens.ask: Consecutive even integers: the difference between two consecutive even integers is ___
screens.why:
Consecutive even integers follow one another: 32, 34, 36, …
Between them sits one odd number: 32, 33, 34.
So each is 2 more than the one before: 34 − 32 = 2.

screens.text: Even and odd results: even + odd + even = ?
screens.why:
Work two at a time, left to right.
even + odd = odd.
odd + even = odd.
Example: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9, which is odd.

screens.text: Even and odd results: odd − even − odd + odd = ?
screens.why:
Go left to right, two at a time.
odd − even = odd.
odd − odd = even.
even + odd = odd.
Example: 5 − 2 − 3 + 1 = 1, which is odd.
screens.clue: Go left to right, two at a time.

Look at the unit digit of each number.
5568 ends in 8 and 1034 ends in 4: even.
−3675 ends in 5, −7109 in 9, −1807 in 7: odd.
The minus sign does not matter.
items.title: Even or odd? Sort each integer.

items.ask: Zero: an even integer which is neither positive nor negative: ___
items.why:
Only one integer is neither positive nor negative: 0.
0 ÷ 2 = 0 with no remainder.
So 0 is even.

items.ask: Positive even integers: the smallest positive even integer is ___
items.why:
The positive integers start 1, 2, 3, …
1 is odd: 1 ÷ 2 leaves remainder 1.
2 is even: 2 ÷ 2 = 1, no remainder.
So the smallest positive even integer is 2.

items.ask: Negative odd integers: the greatest odd negative integer is ___
items.why:
Negative integers: −1, −2, −3, …
The greatest is closest to 0: −1.
−1 ends in 1, so it is odd.
So the answer is −1.

items.ask: Three-digit integers: the greatest three-digit positive integer is ___
items.why:
Three-digit numbers go from 100 to 999.
The greatest has 9 in every place: 999.
999 + 1 = 1000 has four digits.
items.clue: Which is the largest with three digits?

items.text: Even and odd results: even + even = ?
items.why:
Try an example: 2 + 4 = 6.
6 ends in 6, so it is even.
Pairs added to pairs are still pairs. So even + even = even.

items.text: Even and odd results: even − odd = ?
items.why:
Try an example: 12 − 5 = 7.
7 ends in 7, so it is odd.
Taking an odd number from pairs leaves 1 over. So even − odd = odd.

items.text: Even and odd results: odd × odd × even = ?
items.why:
odd × odd = odd.
odd × even = even.
One even factor makes the whole product even.
Example: 3 × 5 × 2 = 30, even.

items.text: Even and odd results: even × odd + even = ?
items.why:
Multiply first: even × odd = even.
Then add: even + even = even.
Example: 2 × 3 + 4 = 6 + 4 = 10, even.

items.ask: Consecutive odd integers: the difference between two consecutive odd integers is ___
items.why:
Consecutive odd integers follow one another: 5, 7, 9, …
Between them sits one even number: 5, 6, 7.
So 7 − 5 = 2.

test.text: Even or odd: is −1807 even or odd?
test.why:
Look at the unit digit: −1807 ends in 7.
7 is one of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
So −1807 is odd.

test.text: Even and odd results: odd + odd = ?
test.why:
Try an example: 3 + 5 = 8.
8 ends in 8, so it is even.
The two leftover 1s make a pair. So odd + odd = even.

test.text: Even integers: tap every even integer.
test.why:
Look at the unit digit.
−36 ends in 6, 0 is 0, −180 ends in 0: even.
55 ends in 5 and 103 ends in 3: odd.

test.text: Odd integers between two numbers: tap all odd integers between −106 and −96.
test.why:
−106 is even, so the first odd integer after it is −105.
Add 2 each time: −105, −103, −101, −99, −97.
The next one, −95, is past −96, so stop.
−104 is even, so leave it out.

test.text: Even and odd results: the product of any three odd integers is
test.why:
odd × odd = odd.
odd × odd = odd again.
So odd × odd × odd = odd.
Example: 3 × 5 × 7 = 105, odd.
